concept.name: On-balance volume
concept.definition: Joe Granville's cumulative volume indicator (Granville's New Key to Stock Market Profits, 1963): a running total that adds the period's volume when the close rises and subtracts it when the close falls, tracking cumulative buying versus selling pressure.
concept.intuition: Granville's thesis is that volume precedes price - if volume consistently flows in on up days, the OBV line rises even before price breaks out.
concept.mechanics: OBV_t = OBV_{t-1} + volume when close_t > close_{t-1}, minus volume when lower, unchanged when equal. The absolute level is meaningless; the line's trend, divergences from price, and support/resistance breaks are the signals.
concept.formula: OBV_t = OBV_{t-1} + sign(C_t - C_{t-1}) x V_t (no change when closes are equal).
concept.failure_modes: A single huge-volume day permanently shifts the line, distorting later readings; it ignores intraday position, so a gap-down day closing near its high still counts as all-negative volume.
concept.misconceptions: OBV's absolute value is not meaningful - only its direction and pattern matter; and a rising OBV does not guarantee price will follow.
concept.example: From OBV 100,000: an up close on 8,200 shares takes it to 108,200, and a subsequent down day on 6,000 shares brings it to 102,200.
